messages:
Maya: Heads-up — planning to lift pin on runtime v3.0.0-beta for a controlled night shift roll tonight 00:30 UTC. Primary motivator: improved kernel scheduling for long-contexts. tagging @Tomas @Priya for compat and rollback plan.
Tomas: Question: does v3.0 change the model ABI for KV cache tokens? A recent model upload showed a header version bump. Need to confirm model bindings.
Priya: I ran model-bind tests vs the canary model set — most pass but we saw 1 failure on bigrams storage serialization. Filing quick fix in runtime repo (PR #987).
Deploybot: Roll window created: 2026-03-26T00:30:00Z -> cohorts: 3% (00:30) -> 15% (01:00) -> 40% (01:30) -> 100% (02:30). Auto-checks: health, p95, embed-contract.
Maya: Rollback criteria: sustained error_rate > 0.8% for 10m OR embed contract v2 mismatch. Manual abort also allowed by infra.
InfraBot: Pre-deploy check OK: cluster capacity, host patch-level. Noted: one us-west-2 host with old kernel image — recommend excluding from first cohort.
Tomas: If embed contract fails, fallback = route embeddings to modelpool:legacy-embed (route toggle ready). I'll coordinate a canary-only toggle to avoid global impact.
Priya: Also note SDK 3.2.0 adds a new Accept header normalization; older SDKs could get 406 on some embed calls. We should update release notes and pin a compatibility shim in the ingress.
Maya: Can we hotpatch ingress? Priya, Tomas — can you prepare the shim and a revert plan?
Priya: Pushed ingress-shim PR #759. It normalizes Accept headers and returns legacy fallback header. Tested in staging.
Deploybot: Canary cohort=3% started (automated). region=us-west-2 hosts=6.
Tomas: 00:39 UTC — small tail latency bump on cold starts (p95 +35ms) for the cohort; could be kvcache warmup. Watching.
Priya: 00:45 UTC — embed contract probe failed for 2 requests (schema mismatch). Triggering fallback to legacy route for embeddings on cohort hosts. Command issued.
Deploybot: Fallback applied: embeddings routed to modelpool:legacy-embed for cohort hosts. (automated)
Maya: Good catch. Keep an eye on error counts; if error_rate recovers, we can continue.
Tomas: 00:55 UTC — error rate steady at 0.6%, p95 back to baseline after warmup. Propose continue to 15% at 01:00.
Maya: Proceeding to step 2. Remember: if we observe any OOMs or native crashes, we abort immediately.
Deploybot: Proceeding to 15% cohort (automated). region=us-east-1 + us-west-2 total hosts=28.
InfraBot: Alert: one host exceeded memory threshold during ramp; container restarted once. Not OOM yet but flagged.
Priya: 01:12 UTC — we see intermittent 502s from one AZ proxy tied to shim timeouts. Increasing shim timeout and redeploying proxy config.
Maya: If 502s persist after 5m, we auto-pinback and open ENG-5421. Who takes rollback? Tomas?
Tomas: I'll handle pinback ops. Rollback commands (if needed):
```
# pinback routing to runtime:v2.28 for affected cohorts
kubectl apply -f routing/pinback-v2-28.yaml --context=prod
# un-deploy canary via deploybot
deploybot cancel --deployment-id 2900001111 --scope=canary
```
Deploybot: Health monitor reported error_rate=1.1% sustained for 7m in us-east-1. Auto-pinback triggered for cohort=15% -> routing to runtime:v2.28. (automated)
Maya: Confirming automated pinback executed. Creating ENG-5421 for investigation: include shim timeout, kvcache warmup, and serialization fix follow-up.
Priya: Collected debug traces and proxy logs, attaching to ENG-5421. Will backport Accept-normalization shim to ingress main branch.
Tomas: We'll target a re-roll after fixes and another smaller night window. Recommend adding explicit kvcache cold-start telemetry to the canary checklist.
Maya: Agreed. Thanks all for quick response. Postmortem/next steps: add stronger embed contract gating, land runtime PR #987, ingress-shim backport, and schedule re-roll. :thanks:
